mission: Convergence Analysis is a nonprofit that does strategic research and advocacy to reduce existential risk from AI. It writes reports on likely AI scenarios and on which governance strategies matter most, and runs AI awareness work for policymakers and the public. Its approach is interdisciplinary, drawing on philosophy, computer science, sociology and psychology.

key_work.title: The AI Readiness Objectives
key_work.plain_summary: Seven broad goals that a government's AI security strategy should meet to be ready for the most powerful AI systems.

key_work.title: AI Model Registries: A Foundational Tool for AI Governance
key_work.plain_summary: Argues governments should keep a register of advanced AI models so they know what exists before they try to regulate it.

key_work.title: AI Emergency Preparedness
key_work.plain_summary: Examines whether the US government could detect and respond quickly to an AI-related national-security emergency.

key_work.title: AI Clarity: An Initial Research Agenda
key_work.plain_summary: Sets out Convergence's scenario-planning agenda: mapping plausible AI futures to find the most important governance interventions.

key_work.title: 2024 State of the AI Regulatory Landscape
key_work.plain_summary: An overview of how the US, China and the EU were regulating AI as of May 2024.

warnings.text: Frontier AI may bring abilities dangerous enough to induce existential outcomes such as civilisational collapse, nuclear warfare or pandemics.
Governments may lack the ability to detect and respond to fast-moving AI national-security threats.

recommendations.text: Model AI scenarios systematically to identify the most important and neglected governance strategies.
Create AI model registries as a foundation for regulation.
Improve government AI emergency preparedness and national AI security strategies.
Raise public and policymaker awareness of critical governance strategies.
